solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Ease of life with Attica becoming decadent

indicators.note: decadent suggests decay and disorder, so the letters of the two words fall into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A lament that the easy life has made the ancient region of Attica soft and decadent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'becoming decadent' tells you to rearrange LIFE and ATTICA together.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease a process is to make it simpler or smoother, a direct verb synonym.

clue.text: Factory's first exercise to produce safety device

indicators.note: first means the opening letter of the word is taken

parts.note: to exercise something, such as a right, is to use it

explanation.surface: A factory's first job is to make a safety component.
explanation.walkthrough: F is the first letter of 'Factory's', then USE.
explanation.definitionFit: A fuse protects an electrical circuit by breaking when the current is too high.

clue.text: Awful rioters following church singer

indicators.note: following places the rearranged letters after the church abbreviation
awful suggests a mess, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Terrible rioters chasing a church singer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awful' is the anagram signal, and 'following' puts the result after the church abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A chorister is a member of a choir, especially a church choir.

clue.text: Learner heading in one direction — to the lowest degree

indicators.note: heading says the learner comes at the head of the word

parts.note: L stands for learner, as on a learner driver's plate
east is one compass direction

explanation.surface: A learner driver going one way, barely at all.
explanation.walkthrough: L is a learner, from the L-plates on a learner driver's car.
explanation.definitionFit: Least is the superlative of little, meaning in the smallest amount or degree.

clue.text: Queen being in a spot creates row

indicators.note: being in says the queen goes inside the other word

parts.note: a trace is a spot or tiny amount
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: The Queen in a difficult spot causes a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' suggests a quarrel but means a line of houses; 'being in' is the container signal. ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrace is a row of houses joined together, a common British style of housing.

clue.text: A number of hill-workers who rent accommodation?

parts.note: ten is a number
ants are workers in an anthill

explanation.surface: How many hill labourers rent their lodgings?
explanation.walkthrough: Ants live and work in hills; ten of them makes TEN ANTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenants are people who rent accommodation from a landlord.

clue.text: Description a tiny bit inadequate

indicators.note: inadequate means falling short, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a speck is a tiny bit or particle

explanation.surface: A complaint that a written description is just a little lacking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inadequate' cuts the last letter, K, from SPECK.
explanation.definitionFit: A spec, short for specification, is a detailed description of what is required.

clue.text: Gather soil conditioner that's left for collection

indicators.note: for collection says the conditioner collects, or takes in, the letter

parts.note: peat is used to improve soil

explanation.surface: Gather up the leftover soil improver for pick-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for collection' puts L inside PEAT.
explanation.definitionFit: To pleat fabric is to gather it into folds.

clue.text: See buildings in various cities

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese, and its principal church stands in a city

explanation.surface: An invitation to go sightseeing among buildings in different cities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like a verb but is a noun: a bishop's see.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop's see is centred on its principal church, which stands in the city.

clue.text: Arrogant idiot being angry, not the first

parts.note: an ass is a fool

indicators.note: not the first means the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: fuming means very angry

explanation.surface: A fool, haughty and furious, comes second.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not the first' drops F from FUMING.
explanation.definitionFit: Assuming as an adjective means presumptuous or taking too much on oneself.

clue.text: Opening boy's found in army

indicators.note: found in says the boy is placed inside the army

parts.note: SA is the Salvation Army
Tom is a boy's name; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: A lad's big opportunity turns out to be joining the army.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' is the container signal; the army here is the Salvation Army, often abbreviated in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoma is a small opening or pore, as on a leaf or made surgically in the body.

clue.text: Becoming active again, being more rational about money

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: more rational means saner
a cent is a small coin, a piece of money

explanation.surface: Someone getting back into action by becoming more sensible about finance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning' but signals a reversal of the word for more rational.
explanation.definitionFit: Renascent means being reborn or reviving, so coming back to life and activity.

clue.text: Seize vehicle going to hellish location

indicators.note: going to says the vehicle is attached after the hellish place

parts.note: Dis is the classical underworld, the infernal city in Dante
a train is a vehicle

explanation.surface: Someone grabbing a train bound for somewhere infernal.
explanation.walkthrough: DIS is a name for the underworld in classical myth and Dante's Inferno.
explanation.definitionFit: To distrain is the legal act of seizing goods to cover a debt.

clue.text: Set adrift, relation's first to go

indicators.note: first to go means the opening letter is removed

parts.note: an auntie is a relation

explanation.surface: A boat cut loose, with a relative the first to depart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first to go' takes A off AUNTIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Untying a boat's mooring rope releases it to drift away.

clue.text: Desperate solution that lies at the end of the package tour?

definitions.meaning: the course taken when all others have failed

definitions.text: that lies at the end of the package tour?
definitions.meaning: the final holiday destination on a trip

explanation.surface: Taking a package holiday as a desperate final option.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes 'resort' as a holiday town, the final stop of the tour.
explanation.definitionFit: When every other option fails you turn to your final recourse, and a tour's final stop is its closing holiday town.

clue.text: It could be the section of a legal document

definitions.meaning: in grammar 'the' is the definite ..., one of a class of words
a numbered clause of a treaty or contract

explanation.surface: Musing on which part of a legal document something might be.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading treats 'the' as a word of grammar, not as part of the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammar names 'the' an article, and contracts and treaties are divided into numbered articles.

clue.text: Conservative smartie, terrible person of some craft

indicators.note: terrible suggests something wrecked, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dreadful Tory clever-clogs who is also something of a craftsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' rearranges SMARTIE into ERAMIST.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceramist is a potter, someone skilled in the craft of making ceramics.

clue.text: Spider? First glimpse of such somewhere in Middlesex

indicators.note: the first glimpse of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: Pinner is a suburb in the old county of Middlesex, north-west London

explanation.surface: Catching sight of a spider somewhere in Middlesex.
explanation.walkthrough: PINNER is a suburb of north-west London, in the historic county of Middlesex.
explanation.definitionFit: A spider spins webs, so it is a spinner; the question mark flags this playful description.

clue.text: Fool, one of the ancient people reportedly, was overcritical

parts.note: a nit, short for nitwit, is a fool

indicators.note: reportedly means the word is as heard, not as written

parts.note: a Pict was one of the ancient people of Scotland

explanation.surface: A fool, one of the ancient tribes, was too fussy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' gives PICKED, which is said the same as PICT, one of the ancient people of northern Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: To nitpick is to find fault over trivial details, to be overly critical.

clue.text: Fighters in the ring feeling pain languish on return

indicators.note: on return means the two words are read backwards together

parts.note: sore means feeling pain
to rot is to languish or waste away

explanation.surface: Boxers in the ring, hurt and wilting as they come back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on return' reverses SOREROT as a whole. The 'ring' is a bullring, not a boxing ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Toreros are bullfighters, who fight in the bullring.

clue.text: Singer thus needs instrument that's right for one

parts.note: so means thus, in this way

indicators.note: right for one means the letter for right replaces the letter that looks like one

parts.note: a piano is a musical instrument

explanation.surface: A singer accordingly needs the right instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right for one' replaces I (one, as a Roman numeral) in PIANO with R, giving PRANO.
explanation.definitionFit: A soprano is a singer with the highest female or boy's voice.

clue.text: Enjoy modern technology, man — it's this!

parts.note: to dig something is slang for enjoying it
taken as the word it
Al is a man's name

explanation.surface: An enthusiast urging a friend to embrace modern technology.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'Dig it, Al': enjoy it, man.
explanation.definitionFit: Digital describes electronic computing technology, the hallmark of the modern age.

clue.text: Active folk holding jollies, as seen from windows

indicators.note: holding means the active folk contain the other letters

parts.note: doers are active people who get things done
Jollies is a nickname for Royal Marines, abbreviated RM

explanation.surface: Busy people having fun, as viewed from the window.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jollies' is not fun here: Jollies is an old slang name for the Royal Marines. 'holding' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Dormers are upright windows set into a sloping roof.

clue.text: Poems about Surrey town

indicators.note: about suggests moving things around, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Verses written about a town in Surrey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' tells you to rearrange POEMS. EPSOM is a Surrey town famous for its racecourse and the Derby.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsom is a market town in Surrey, south of London, home of the Derby horse race.

clue.text: Quiet little person may have to bear many things

definitions.text: may have to bear many things

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet
an elf is a small sprite

explanation.surface: A quiet little person who has a lot to put up with.
explanation.definitionFit: A shelf supports and holds up many objects placed on it.

clue.text: Occasional table for scientist may be so described

definitions.meaning: happening from time to time, at intervals

definitions.text: table for scientist may be so described
definitions.meaning: the chart of chemical elements a chemist uses has this name

explanation.surface: An occasional table, a piece of furniture, as a scientist might describe it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Occasional table' looks like furniture; the words split into two separate readings.
explanation.definitionFit: Recurring at intervals means occasional, and Mendeleev's chart of elements bears the name.

clue.text: Men getting worried speak at length?

parts.note: OR, other ranks, are soldiers who are not officers
ate, as in 'what's eating you', means worried

explanation.surface: Anxious men talk on and on.
explanation.walkthrough: OR means other ranks, ordinary soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to deliver a speech, often a long and pompous one.

clue.text: One observes a channel partially hollowed out

indicators.note: partially hollowed out means an inner letter is removed

parts.note: a sewer is a channel for waste water

explanation.surface: A viewer notices a channel has been partly dug out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partially hollowed out' removes W from the middle of SEWER.
explanation.definitionFit: A seer is literally one who sees, as well as a prophet.

clue.text: Exaggerate position of country's ruler

definitions.meaning: to overdo or inflate in describing
a ruler stands over the state

explanation.surface: Overplaying how important a nation's leader's role is.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as OVER STATE for the second reading: where a ruler sits.
explanation.definitionFit: To exaggerate is to claim more than the truth, to overdo a description.

clue.text: Seen in park, legendary horse winning many races

indicators.note: seen in says the letters are found within the following words

explanation.surface: A famous racehorse spotted in a park.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seen in' shows the letters inside 'park, legendary'. Arkle was a celebrated Irish steeplechaser of the 1960s, winner of three Cheltenham Gold Cups.
explanation.definitionFit: Arkle was an Irish steeplechaser who won three Cheltenham Gold Cups and many other races.

clue.text: President getting behind after short time

indicators.note: after places the word for behind following the short time

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
aft means behind, at the stern of a ship

explanation.surface: A leader falling behind after only a brief spell in office.
explanation.definitionFit: William Howard Taft was the 27th President of the United States.

clue.text: The Spanish dealer's in trouble — what can attract customers?

parts.note: los is a Spanish word for the

indicators.note: in trouble suggests something disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Spanish trader in difficulty wonders how to draw in shoppers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in trouble' rearranges DEALERS into SLEADER.
explanation.definitionFit: A loss leader is an item sold cheaply at a loss to draw shoppers into a store.
